gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on 2026-11-14 BLUETTI's own AC180 + 2×200 W kit ($1,232) costs $64 more than buying the AC180 + 200 W kit ($769) and adding a loose BLUETTI 200 W panel ($399) for $1,168, so here the bigger bundle is the worse buy.
standout_why: I compared against StormWatts (cited), GetWattLogic (cited), Trek4Tech and Powersized. StormWatts (prices checked 2026-10-16, page updated 2026-11-08) still lists AC180 + 2×200 W at $949 and says the bigger kit is 'the better value per watt on both stores' because the second panel cost only $180 more. Today the gap between the 1-panel and 2-panel kits is $463, which is more than the panel's $399 standalone price. Powersized has the $1,232 price but only compares it with all-separate parts ($1,297, so a $65 saving). It never compares it with the 1-panel kit plus a loose panel. GetWattLogic and Trek4Tech give no prices.
decides: This backs the 'compare totals' advice and makes it sharper. The cheapest bundle is not always the biggest one. A BLUETTI AC180 buyer who wants 400 W of panels should buy the 200 W kit and add one panel ($1,168), not the 2-panel kit ($1,232). On the Elite 200 V2 it goes the other way. The 2×200 W kit ($1,499) beats the 1-panel kit plus a loose panel ($1,598), and it is the better buy for a 2,080 Wh battery. GetWattLogic's rule is panel watts ≥ battery Wh ÷ 3, which comes to about 690 W. So the answer is to price three totals: the kit, the kit plus a loose panel, and the station plus a panel.
